name: Kathmandu
tagline: Himalayan Culture and Adventure at Rock-Bottom Costs
description: Kathmandu is a city of ancient temples, stunning mountain views, and one of the lowest costs of living in the world. Nestled in a valley surrounded by the Himalayas, it offers a unique blend of Hindu and Buddhist culture, world-class trekking, and a growing modern infrastructure. For FIRE seekers willing to embrace a different pace of life, Kathmandu delivers extraordinary value and unforgettable experiences.

quickFacts.visa: Visa on arrival (15/30/90 days), extendable up to 150 days per year. Non-tourist visas available for those with Nepali investments. No dedicated retirement visa — tourist visa cycling is the norm for long-term retirees.
quickFacts.language: Nepali, with some English in tourist areas
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – generally safe; watch for petty theft and traffic
quickFacts.climate: Subtropical with monsoon season and cool winters

housing.description: Small semi-furnished private 1BR/studio in an ordinary residential area (Koteshwor / Baneshwor / Kalanki edge), not the expat belt

dining.description: Mostly home-cooked; occasional dal bhat / momo at local eateries

healthcare.description: Pay-as-you-go outpatient visits at private clinics like Norvic and Grande, plus a basic local policy covering hospital stays; priced for an early retiree aged 45-55.

entertainment.description: Occasional QFX cinema, budget gym, a local weekend trek

1M.lifestyle: A small furnished apartment in an ordinary residential neighborhood like Baneshwor or Koteshwor, away from the pricier expat belt, with home cooking supplemented by dal bhat and momos at local eateries. Microbuses and the occasional Pathao or InDrive ride cover daily movement. Out-of-pocket clinic visits plus a basic local hospitalization policy handle health needs, and valley hikes and budget treks are cheap and close at hand. Air pollution, winter cold, and chaotic traffic are the real daily tradeoffs, but the cost base is remarkably low.

housing.description: Large 3BR house or apartment in Budhanilkantha or Sanepa with garden

dining.description: Mix of upscale restaurants in Durbarmarg and Thamel; international cuisine options

healthcare.description: Premium private insurance with medical evacuation coverage to Delhi or Bangkok

transportation.description: Own motorbike or small car; occasional domestic flights to Pokhara

entertainment.description: Guided treks, rafting trips, mountain biking, cultural festivals, regular Pokhara getaways

2M.lifestyle: A decent furnished apartment near the expat-friendly neighborhoods of Kupondole or Pulchowk, with regular local meals and the occasional mid-range restaurant. Ride-hailing covers most trips, and a local private health policy plus self-pay clinic visits handle routine care. A gym, cafe outings, and the occasional getaway fit the budget, with a comfortable cushion at Kathmandu's low costs.

housing.description: Furnished modern 1BR in the expat-favored belt (Jhamsikhel / Sanepa / Lazimpat)

dining.description: Frequent mid-range restaurants + expat cafes in Jhamsikhel/Thamel

healthcare.description: Mid local policy (cashless at Indian hospitals) + comfortable self-pay at top private hospitals

transportation.description: Daily Pathao/InDrive rides, occasional taxi, or own-scooter fuel

entertainment.description: Gym, cinema, cafes, weekend trips / trekking

3M.lifestyle: A furnished modern apartment in the expat-favored belt of Jhamsikhel, Sanepa, or Lazimpat, with regular meals out at mid-range restaurants and the well-known cafe scene, and grocery runs to Bhatbhateni for imported goods. Daily ride-hailing or an owned scooter covers transport. A mid-level local health policy plus comfortable self-pay access to the top private hospitals removes the main worry. A gym, a cafe habit, and frequent weekend trekking all fit, with clear margin left over at Kathmandu's prices.

housing.description: Sprawling estate in Budhanilkantha or custom-built villa with panoramic Himalayan views

dining.description: Private chef plus regular dining at Kathmandu's finest restaurants and hotels

healthcare.description: VIP concierge medical service with Singapore and Bangkok hospital access

transportation.description: Luxury SUV with driver, regular domestic flights, helicopter charters

entertainment.description: Private Everest expeditions, luxury lodge trekking, international travel, cultural patronage

domesticHelp.description: Full-time cook, housekeeper, gardener, driver, and security guard

luxuryExtras.description: First-class international travel, luxury trekking expeditions, philanthropy, property investments

5M.lifestyle: A spacious furnished home in the expat belt — Jhamsikhel, Baluwatar, or Sanepa — with a part-time housekeeper-cook and an owned car or heavy premium ride-hailing. Frequent upscale dining and hotel restaurants, a premium imported grocery basket, and health cover trending toward international-grade plans. Club memberships, domestic travel, and lodge-based trekking are easily absorbed, and Nepal's low local costs leave a wide monthly margin.

housing.description: Large furnished house with garden, diplomatic-grade, in Budhanilkantha / Maharajgunj / Baluwatar

dining.description: Top restaurants + five-star hotel dining (Dwarika's etc.)

healthcare.description: International / evacuation-grade cover with Delhi/Bangkok/Singapore access

transportation.description: Private SUV ownership, fuel, maintenance (driver salaried under domesticHelp)

luxuryExtras.description: International travel, imported luxury goods, private club memberships

10M.lifestyle: A large diplomatic-grade house with a garden in Budhanilkantha, Maharajgunj, or Baluwatar, staffed by a live-in housekeeper-cook, a driver, and part-time garden and security help. A private SUV handles mountain roads, and international health cover — with medical evacuation to Delhi, Bangkok, or Singapore — is the key safeguard given Kathmandu's thin local tertiary care. Dining reaches the city's best restaurants and five-star hotels, though the fine-dining scene is genuinely limited, and premium imports carry a real markup. Club memberships, luxury lodge-based trekking, and frequent international travel fill out the budget. Nepal's thin luxury market caps how much can be spent locally, so this level typically keeps a Kathmandu base for Himalayan access and travels widely.
